chunks: And from him, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from Aban, from Muhammad, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): In

A man married a woman, and she stayed with him for a few days during which he was unable to have intercourse with her, except that he had seen from her that which is forbidden for men [to see]. Then he divorced her, and she had a daughter. He said: 'It is not permissible for him to marry her daughter, since he had seen from her that which he had seen.'

key_terms.لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُهَا: he was unable to have intercourse with her
key_terms.لاَ يَصْلُحُ لَهُ: it is not permissible for him
key_terms.مَا يَحْرُمُ عَلَى الرِّجَالِ: that which is forbidden for men

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his ex-wife's daughter if he divorced her after seeing her private parts but before consummation?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a specific impediment of 'seeing' (ru'yah) distinct from consummation, prohibiting a man from marrying the daughter of a woman whose private parts he viewed during their brief marriage. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the significance of the husband's visual access to the wife's 'awrah' as a barrier to affinity, even in the absence of sexual intercourse. The hadith underscores the legal weight of physical intimacy beyond mere contract, reflecting the detailed nuances of family law in the Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
